A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 17-page MolParser paper, including the six-page supplementary material. Full-text comparison and rendering of every page support reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v3 reports original recognition accuracy and throughput, ablation experiments, and molecular property prediction results in Tables 2–6, plus supplementary qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: v4 retains the original experimental results in Tables 2–6 and the supplementary qualitative evaluations.

M1.justification: The E-SMILES representation, Swin/MLP/BART architecture, curriculum training, and active-learning data engine are identical in Sections 3–4 and the supplement.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same training sources, OCSR benchmarks including both WildMol subsets, five MoleculeNet classification tasks, and reaction-parsing examples.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 retain exactly the same OCSR comparators, including DECIMER 2.7, MolScribe, and MolGrapher. The property-prediction comparator set in Table 6 is also unchanged.

E3.justification: Dataset sizes, model variants and resolutions, evaluation metrics, throughput measurements, augmentations, and training schedules match throughout Sections 6, 10.2, and 11.

E4.justification: The data-scale, fine-tuning, model-scale, augmentation, and curriculum analyses in Section 6.3 and Tables 3–5 are unchanged. Figures 9–11 retain the same qualitative successes and failures.

E5.justification: Table 6 reports average ROC-AUC over five runs in both versions. Repeated-run and uncertainty reporting is otherwise identical, with no added seeds, intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative findings match. For example, MolParser-Base retains 76.9% WildMol-10K accuracy, 38.1% WildMol-10K-M accuracy, and throughput of 39.8 images per second in Tables 2–3.

T1.justification: The E-SMILES definitions and indexing rules in Sections 3.1 and 9 are identical. Neither version contains theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain identical claims about E-SMILES, MolParser-7M, WildMol, recognition performance, processing speed, and downstream utility.

C2.justification: Interpretations of fine-tuning, scaling, and molecular representations are unchanged. Both retain the chirality limitation in Section 7 and the failure conditions and unsupported structures in Section 12 and Figures 10–11.

D1.justification: Sections 8, 10.2, and 11 retain the same dataset/model/demo access links, augmentation instructions, architecture details, optimization settings, and hardware information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 70 reference entries are identical. Research positioning and relationships to prior methods are unchanged.

P1.justification: v4 corrects the first-page author name from 'Shangqian Che' to 'Shangqian Chen' and updates the arXiv version/date stamp. All other wording and section organization are identical.

P2.justification: All six tables, twelve figures, captions, and placements are unchanged. Pages 2–17 render identically; first-page differences are confined to author-line and arXiv-stamp text.

improvement.justification: The author-name correction improves attribution accuracy, but the only other change is the arXiv stamp. Scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and substantive presentation remain identical, so overall paper quality does not meaningfully change.
